lba_qa.q: A circular garden has a radius of 7 m. Find its area so the gardener knows how much grass seed to buy. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Area of a circle = pi x r^2.
Area = (22/7) x 7 x 7 = 22 x 7 = 154 square metres.
So the area of the circular garden is 154 sq m, and the gardener needs grass seed for 154 sq m.

lba_qa.q: A circular track has a radius of 21 m. A runner wants to know the distance of one full round. Find the circumference. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Circumference = 2 x pi x r.
= 2 x (22/7) x 21 = 2 x 22 x 3 = 132 metres.
So one full round of the track is 132 metres.

lba_qa.q: A pizza of radius 14 cm is cut into a slice (sector) with an angle of 90 degrees. Find the area of one slice. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Area of a sector = (angle/360) x pi x r^2.
= (90/360) x (22/7) x 14 x 14.
= (1/4) x (22/7) x 196 = (1/4) x 616 = 154 sq cm.
So the area of one 90-degree pizza slice is 154 sq cm.

lba_qa.q: A goat is tied to a peg with a 7 m rope in a field. Over how much grassy area can the goat graze? (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
The goat can move in a circle of radius equal to the rope length (7 m).
Grazing area = area of circle = pi x r^2 = (22/7) x 7 x 7 = 154 sq m.
So the goat can graze over an area of 154 square metres.

lba_qa.q: A clock's minute hand is 7 cm long. Find the area swept by the minute hand in 15 minutes. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
In 15 minutes, the minute hand sweeps 1/4 of the full circle (15/60 = 1/4), which is an angle of 90 degrees.
Area swept = (angle/360) x pi x r^2 = (90/360) x (22/7) x 7 x 7.
= (1/4) x (22/7) x 49 = (1/4) x 154 = 38.5 sq cm.
So the minute hand sweeps an area of 38.5 sq cm in 15 minutes.

lba_qa.q: A circular flower bed of radius 14 m is surrounded by a path. If we want the area of just the flower bed, what formula do we use and what is the area? (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Area of the circular flower bed = pi x r^2.
= (22/7) x 14 x 14 = 22 x 28 = 616 sq m.
So the area of the flower bed is 616 square metres.

lba_qa.q: A wire is bent into a circle of radius 7 cm. If the same wire is now bent into a square, what is the perimeter of the square? (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
The length of the wire = circumference of the circle = 2 x pi x r = 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 cm.
When bent into a square, the perimeter of the square = same wire length = 44 cm.
So the perimeter of the square is 44 cm (each side = 44/4 = 11 cm).

lba_qa.q: The area of a sector of a circle depends on its central angle. Explain how a half circle (semicircle) and a quarter circle relate to the full circle's area.
lba_qa.a:
The area of a sector = (angle/360) x area of full circle.
A semicircle has a central angle of 180 degrees, so its area = (180/360) = 1/2 of the full circle's area.
A quarter circle has 90 degrees, so its area = (90/360) = 1/4 of the full circle's area.
So the sector area is a fraction of the full circle based on the angle.

lba_qa.q: A circular plate has a diameter of 28 cm. Find its area. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
First find the radius: radius = diameter/2 = 28/2 = 14 cm.
Area = pi x r^2 = (22/7) x 14 x 14 = 22 x 28 = 616 sq cm.
So the area of the plate is 616 sq cm.

lba_qa.q: A circular pond of radius 14 m is surrounded by a 7 m wide path. Find the area of the path. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Outer radius = 14 + 7 = 21 m; inner radius = 14 m.
Area of path = area of outer circle - area of inner circle = pi(R^2 - r^2).
= (22/7)(21^2 - 14^2) = (22/7)(441 - 196) = (22/7)(245) = 22 x 35 = 770 sq m.
So the area of the path is 770 square metres.
